title: Where Is Thy Sting, O Death
description: Where Is Thy Sting, O Death in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 349, “O Death, Where Is Thy Sting?”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Where is thy sting, O death? Grave! where thy vic-to-ry? The clod may sleep in dust be-neath, The spir-it will be free!

lines: Where is thy sting, O death?
The clod may sleep in dust beneath,
Both man and time have power
But death arrives, and in that hour
Then, death, where is thy sting?
O'er your dark bourn the soul will spring
To Him who loves to save.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
